frontier.hypothesis: Cluster B closes if $v0 can be made dead in mark_target_live_regs(insn 731) - and the trace already shows that live set is over-approximate ($a3 is marked live there and is provably dead), so the C dial is the SHAPE of the fall-through 0x19/0xB selection block and of the first 0xE test that also branches to its label.
frontier.mechanism: reorg.c computes basic_block_live_at_start once and mark_target_live_regs returns it verbatim when the target IS the block head. Block 27 begins at code_label 347, whose own first action is to SET $v0, so a correct live-in would exclude $v0. The over-approximation must come either from label 347 having a second predecessor (the `bnez $v0` of the first 0xE test branches there too) or from the block head having moved when sched2 folded `v0 = 0x19` into the `bnez $s1` sequence. Clearing bit 0x4 of oppregs makes insn_sets_resource_p(368, &opposite_needed) return 0, all five predicates pass, and dbr steals `v0 = 1` into the slot exactly as target does - closing cluster B's ~4 points AND the 216-vs-215 insn surplus.
frontier.next_probe: On the base body run `bash tmp/grind/func_800283D0/s18/dbr.sh <tag>` (it writes the DBRDBG log and the -da dumps together) for two restructurings of the `||`: (a) give the first 0xE test its own branch target so label 347 has exactly ONE predecessor, e.g. `if ((u32)(h0-6) >= 2U) { if ((u32)(h1-6) >= 2U) { D_800A38A8 = 1; D_800A3876 = -1; goto block_49; } } var_v0_2 = 0x19; if (var_s1 == 0) var_v0_2 = 0xB; goto block_48;`; (b) spell the selection so its first insn is not the one sched2 folds into the branch sequence. Locate the branch UID by searching tmp/grind/func_800283D0/s18/code6cac_b.i.dbr for the insn setting `(mem (symbol_ref "D_800A38A8"))` and walking back to the preceding jump_insn, then grep the log for `DBRDBG thr insn=<uid>` and read the oppregs word. Bit 0x4 clearing is the win condition; score with `sandbox --disable all` twice.

frontier.hypothesis: On a store-pinned body the byte-free nrefs(73) route is FORECLOSED, and one measurement settles it: E-s18-1's ref map proves only three call-pair sites exist, and find_cross_jump merges TAILS, so only the `<` arm can tail-merge with path1 - the same arm the pin occupies.
frontier.mechanism: jump2 runs after RA (E-s18-6), so a duplicated call pair is free at allocation time and can merge to zero emitted cost - but only if the duplicating block and its partner are scheduled IDENTICALLY (E-s17-5's law, read from BB2_XJUMP_DEBUG). path1's tail is `store; calls; return`; the `==` arm's calls are followed by the `== 5` subtree and the `>` path's by the 0x1A selection, so neither is a tail. That leaves the `<` arm, which on a pinned body is spending its goto on the pin.
frontier.next_probe: Build tD's self-supplied path1 pin (E-s17-6: each selection edge does its own store and the 0xB edge's `goto do_calls` supplies the label; emitted 80-88 is byte-exact) and give the `<` arm a duplicated call pair whose block BEGINS with its own store, so both blocks are scheduled identically per E-s17-5's law. Confirm the seats with s18/al.sh and the merge with BB2_XJUMP_DEBUG=1 (s17/xj_tC.txt is the template trace). If it still stalls at 12/221 like tC/tE/tH, record the nrefs route as FORECLOSED on every pinned body and hand the function's whole remaining budget to cluster B.

frontier.hypothesis: A livelen(143) displacement that costs fewer than 5 diff points would make cluster A free on a pinned body, but no such site exists in this function's shape - the six insns have to come from code target places after the reload.
frontier.mechanism: E-s18-4's ladder is linear and E-s18-5 prices the cheapest crossing at ~10. The only computations available to move are the two 0xE boolean chains and the 0x19/0xB selection, and target emits all three after the `== 5` test; moving the selection additionally triggers a jump2 dedupe of target's two identical 4-insn selection blocks.
frontier.next_probe: Only worth revisiting if frontier item 2 forecloses the nrefs route AND cluster B closes: at that point a body at ~6 with the store pinned would make a 10-point displacement cost worth re-pricing against the unpinned base.
